_note: The Day 3 (Ransomware) work order. Same format as day2_recovery.json. attacks: the Response patterns that got through become these repairs. Components: rebuild (OrderSteps), restore (BackupTimeline, with the 3-2-1 step), folders (PermissionGrid), file_server (the final check, FileServerRepair).

room.controls: WASD / arrows: move     E: use     Esc: pause
room.waiting_body: Response has not confirmed that the ransomware is contained. You can look around, but the equipment must stay dark until it is.
room.all_done: Checks complete. Return to the office entrance to finish.
room.summary_body: The repairs and the final check passed.
room.summary_lesson: Ransomware is beaten by a backup kept apart, from before the infection and tested, and by giving each person only the access the job needs.
room.unknown_damage: Unsupported damage: {ids}. A matching recovery task is needed.
room.verify_locked: Finish the required restoration work before the final access checks.
room.not_required: This equipment does not need restoration in this work order.

comments.clean: Joshua: Everything restored, and not one wrong move. Marta has her report back.
comments.done: Joshua: Everything is restored. Next time, test the backup before you trust it.

task_ui.hint: Take your time. Read the labels before choosing.

case.brief: The ransomware is stopped, but it left a mess. Marta's laptop is sick, the files must come back from a backup, and the shared folders are open to too many people. Fix each one, then check that Marta can work again.
case.lesson: Keep a backup apart from the network, test it, and give each person only the access the job needs.

rebuild.title: Wipe and rebuild the laptop
rebuild.instruction: Marta's laptop is infected. Cleaning it is not enough, so rebuild it. Put the six steps in the right order.
rebuild.lesson: When the damage runs deep, rebuilding beats cleaning. Keep the laptop off the network until it is clean.
rebuild.heading: Rebuild steps
rebuild.pick: Click the first step. Then the next, and so on.
rebuild.wrong: That step is not next yet. Think about what has to happen before it.

steps.label: Unplug it from the network
steps.done: The laptop can no longer reach anything. It cannot spread.
steps.early: Unplug it first. While it is connected, it can still reach the network.

steps.label: Save the files you need, and scan them
steps.done: The files you need are saved and scanned.
steps.early: Save and scan the files before you wipe anything, or they are gone.

steps.label: Reinstall the system from a clean image
steps.done: The laptop is clean. Nothing from before is left on it.
steps.early: Reinstall only after the files are saved, or you wipe them with the rest.

steps.label: Install only approved programs
steps.done: Only approved programs are on the clean laptop.
steps.early: Programs go on the clean system, so reinstall the system first.

steps.label: Restore your files
steps.done: The saved and scanned files are back.
steps.early: Restore the files after the programs, so they open with the right program.

steps.label: Reconnect it to the network
steps.done: The laptop is back on the network, clean.
steps.early: Reconnect last. If you reconnect now, anything left on it can spread again.

rebuild.success: The laptop is rebuilt, clean and back on the network. Nothing of the attack is left on it.

restore.title: Restore from the right backup
restore.instruction: The files are locked, but not the backups kept apart. Pick the newest backup from before the infection that is kept offline and checked. Test it, then restore it.
restore.lesson: The newest backup may carry the infection. A backup nobody tested may not work. There is always a gap.
restore.heading: Backups, oldest to newest
restore.pick: Click a backup to read about it.
restore.choose: Click a backup to read about it.

backups.label:
4 days ago
Shared drive
backups.detail: Four days ago. Kept on the shared drive. Never tested.
backups.bad: This one is old, and nobody tested it. Older is not safer: it may not even work.

backups.label:
01:00
Shared drive
backups.detail: 01:00. Kept on the shared drive, connected to the network. The lock reached it at 09:17.
backups.bad: This copy sat on the shared drive, so the lock reached it too. Its files are locked.

backups.label:
01:00
Offline drive
backups.detail: 01:00. Kept on a drive that was unplugged after the copy. Tested: it restores fine.

backups.label:
09:30
Shared drive
backups.detail: 09:30. Made after the infection, on the shared drive.
backups.bad: This copy was made after the infection. It is a copy of the locked files.

restore.tested: Offline, from before the infection and complete. The restore test passed.
restore.test_first: Test the selected copy before restoring it.
restore.restored: The files are back, exactly as they were at 01:00.
restore.lost: The work between 01:00 and 09:12 is lost, about 8 hours. There is always a gap.
restore.rule_heading: Next time: the 3-2-1 rule. Keep 3 copies, on 2 kinds of storage, 1 of them offline.
restore.rule_empty: Choose where each of the three copies is kept.
restore.rule_one_kind: All three copies are on the same kind of storage. One failure takes them all.
restore.rule_not_offline: None of the copies is offline. A lock on the network reaches all of them.
restore.success: Three copies, on two kinds of storage, one offline. The next attack will not find them all.

folders.title: Reopen the shared folders
folders.instruction: One laptop could reach every folder, and that is how the lock spread. Take away the access a person does not need.
folders.lesson: Give only the access the job needs. Then one account cannot lock everything.
folders.heading: Who may open which folder
folders.pick: Turn off the access a person does not need. Keep what their job needs.
folders.extra: That person does not need this folder. Leave it off.

rows.label: Marta
rows.reason: Marta works in Finance. She needs the Finance folder.

rows.label: Dana
rows.reason: Dana works on designs. She needs the Design folder.

rows.label: Carla
rows.reason: Carla looks after HR files. She needs the HR folder.

folders.success: Everyone has the access their job needs and no more. One account can no longer lock everything.

file_server.title: Back to work
file_server.instruction: Check Marta's work the way she does it every day. Each check proves one repair worked.
file_server.lesson: Recovery is finished only when the person can work normally again and you have checked it.

checks.label: RESTORED FILE
checks.expected: Trusted record: the Finance budget should open, with its usual ending.
checks.passed: The budget opened, and its ending is .xlsx, not .locked.
checks.failed: The budget will not open. Do not mark recovery complete.

checks.label: BACKUP JOB
checks.expected: Trusted record: the backup job should finish.
checks.passed: The backup job finished, and the offline copy was made.
checks.failed: The backup job did not finish. Recovery stays open.

checks.label: FOLDER ACCESS
checks.expected: Trusted record: Marta may write to Finance only.
checks.passed: Marta can write to Finance and nothing else.
checks.failed: Folder access is wrong. Recovery stays open.

file_server.all_checks: Run every check before confirming recovery.
file_server.failed: A check failed. Keep recovery open and ask the response team to address the result.
file_server.success: The budget opened, the backup job ran, and Marta can reach only her folder. She is back to work.

response_outcome.summary: Response contained the ransomware. Marta's laptop, the backups and the shared folders are ready for repairs.
